title: Joining King Swayzee at the Mid-City Theatre and leaving on the road
summary: He joined King Swayzee's jazz band as second trumpet, left on tour without telling his mother, played all summer for almost no pay and dropped out of school.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So all right, then I was at a little dumpy theatre, it's called the Mid-City Theatre, and they had a jazz band in there and they had a fellow named King Swayzee; he come from Arkansas and he looked like one of them -- not Cherokee, like a Pawnee Indian, so King Swayzee, he was in this show and he had a fellow named Eichelberg on the saxophone, had a guy on trombone,
and I said I would like to join this band They needed a second trumpet and said get right in there.
So I was so excited that I just left, just cut out. So then I wrote my mother when I was on the road, went on down to [St.] (Virginia) Petersburg and I was so happy. The man wasn't paying me nothing.

Oh, you know, it's awful the theatre manager, owe for the drops, and I wasn't getting nothing, just enough to eat with, but I was happy, but I was so happy, man, so then we played all that summer. I wrote my mother (unintelligible) and she said what about school and I barely made it, so I just dropped out, just disappeared and then -- but I had gotten that bug and then I was saying, then I heard this Ike Dixon and Ford Dabney then Fletcher Henderson come down and shook everybody up and at that time, now, Duke had just come to New York, so I said my goodness, then Claude Hopkins went to Europe in 1923, see. I think it was Spain or somewhere and Henry Goodman left and when Henry didn't come back, he was telling me (unintelligible)
